- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.  
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often lags; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to match sentiment reversal.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model tends to hold too high; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows volatility, model often fails to capture volatility; add ±1–2% jitter to forecast for next 2–3 periods.
